title: Sable Marine on-prem deploy constraints and tf strategy (draft)
content:
Context:
This is a working draft for Sable Marine's private (on-prem + VPC-peered) inference deployment. Customer has strict egress rules, HSM-backed key management, and a mixed GPU fleet (A100 + T4) at two sites (primary dockside DC in Seattle, warm standby in Portland). They want a predictable 95th percentile latency of <=120ms for 1k RPS baseline with burst to 3k RPS during nightly route optimization windows.

Objective of this doc:
- Capture sizing assumptions and capacity model for both sites
- Surface architecture questions for Sable engineering/security
- Draft Terraform module strategy, remote state and upgrade constraints
- Outline a staged upgrade + rollback plan for initial install and later runtime/quant changes
- Flag known risks and mitigation ideas

High-level topology (proposed):
- Primary site: 8x A100 (80GB) in 2 clusters (inference-pool-a, inference-pool-b), 4x T4 for low-cost embedding/aux tasks
- Standby site: 2x A100 + 4x T4 used for failover and batch rebuilds
- Control plane: customer-managed VPC with peering to Redwood private control-plane-hosted API proxy; option for on-prem control-plane container if customer requires fully airgapped control plane
- Networking: eBPF-based pod-level egress filtering, NAT gateway only for CVM/OS patching windows; mTLS between Redwood agent and control plane
- Secrets/KMS: HSM-backed KMS (Thales/Azure KeyVault/HSM) with PKCS#11 integration for model key wrapping

Sizing rationale and numbers (working):
- Baseline target: 1,000 RPS for small-gen tasks (avg request ~180 tokens). We assume ~0.9 tokens/ms on A100 baseline kernel for seq=512. Using workload mix: 70% short chat (<=256), 20% embeddings, 10% long-gen.
- Inference concurrency and batch sizing: prefer continuous batching; aim for 64-token microbatch with dynamic batching up to 512 depending on latency headroom. For our mixed workload model we estimate each A100 can sustain ~1800 short requests/minute (baseline).
- Capacity recommendation: primary site: 8x A100 -> estimated steady throughput ~240k tokens/sec aggregate, meets baseline latency with 20% headroom; T4s handle embedding & low-cost tasks and absorb background evals. Standby site sized to accept 50% of baseline load within 3 min with autoscaler policy pre-warm.
- Storage: model store on Ceph/S3-compatible backing; model shard bucket per site with lifecycle rule for quantized artifacts. Persistent KV cache stored on local NVMe with periodic checkpoint to S3.

Terraform & infra module notes (constraints + approach):
- Keep modules composable and idempotent: core modules we plan to use: network-vpc, k8s-cluster, gpu-node-pool, storage-s3, kms-integration, redwood-agent, monitoring-alerting.
- State backend: remote state in customer-managed object store (S3-compatible) with Dynamo-style locking service (consul/etcd or Terraform Cloud/TFE if allowed). We must support environments where locking is not available (airgapped) -> document manual state lock process and CI gating.
- Module versioning: version modules semantically (v0.12.0+) and publish changelogs. Upgrades MUST be gated by a plan/approval step and rollout on a canary namespace first.
- Secrets: no plaintext secrets in terraform state. Use external secret injection (vault) and reference by id only. For HSM integration we plan a small terraform module that provisions the KMS alias and initial key policy and outputs the key identifier as a string.
- Cluster upgrades: use node-pool blue/green pattern for GPU nodes to ensure existing long-running pods (with KV cache) are drained gracefully. Controller-manager will prefer pod disruption budgets to avoid mass eviction.

Airgap & egress constraints notes:
- Two allowed egress patterns: (1) scheduled egress windows to allow image pulls from Redwood-managed registry mirrored to customer artifact registry, (2) pre-staged docker images + offline package bundle. For Sable they prefer option 2 for upgrade windows.
- Plan: provide an offline bundle (OCI archive) and a manifest file; Terraform module will optionally install from local registry entrypoint. Document checksum verification step for images.

Upgrade plan (initial install -> v1 -> v1.1 quant/optim changes):
1) Preflight: run infra lint (CIDR overlap, quotas), validate HSM keys and network ACLs, confirm NTP/time sync, run quick load generator at 10% scale for kernel compatibility checks.
2) Initial deploy (v1.0): terraform apply for network & k8s & node pools; install redwood-agent; deploy inference services with model pinned to exact artifact digest; enable monitoring/alerts and cost telemetry.
3) Canary traffic: route 1% traffic to canary pool (different node-pool label) for 24h with traces/latency SLOs monitored.
4) Quantization/optimization rollout (v1.1): deploy optimized quantized model as a second replica set behind canary routing. Run A/B to check quality regression on a curated prompt set.
5) Full rollout and decommission old replica set only after quality metrics and latency within targets.
6) Rollback: terraform module includes a flag to pin to previous model digest and quick re-route via service selector; for infra-level failures, node-pool blue/green and restore from snapshot of NVMe cache where needed.

Open questions for Sable engineering (to resolve ASAP):
- HSM vendor & exact PKCS#11 interface details? Do they allow Redwood's agent to call HSM directly or must calls be proxied through a customer gateway?
- Do we have permission to run an internal NAT for controlled egress during scheduled windows? If not, we must use fully offline bundles only.
- Acceptable RTO/RPO for model-cache warmup on failover? Current design assumes ~3 minutes to warm key-value caches to 70% hit rate.
- Preferred remote state locking mechanism: can we deploy a lightweight Consul cluster, or does policies require Terraform Enterprise?
- Operator constraints: customer prefers k8s 1.27+, any strict OCI runtime constraints?

Known risks and mitigations:
- Mixed GPU types introduces scheduling fragmentation: mitigate by labeling workloads and adding a short-lived conversion job that serializes large requests to A100-only pools.
- KMS latency during cold start if HSM in remote site: add KMS caching layer with short-lived wrapping keys to avoid per-request HSM roundtrip.
- Airgap upgrades increase ops overhead and time-to-patch: propose quarterly scheduled maintenance windows and provide automation for bundle generation.

Action items (next short sprint):
- Asha: finalize module skeletons and post PR to infra-private with example variables for Sable (due 2025-03-07)
- Marco: confirm HSM vendor and collect PKCS#11 test credentials (due 2025-02-28)
- Evelyn: produce offline bundle generation doc & checksum signing steps (due 2025-03-05)
- Priya: run cost model simulation for mixed fleet and submit spreadsheet (linked as artifact) (due 2025-03-04)

Appendix: Terraform quick notes (copy/paste friendly)
- Example pattern for blue/green GPU nodepool:
  module "gpu-node-pool" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//gpu-node-pool?ref=v0.13.1"
    cluster_name = var.cluster_name
    node_labels = { pool = var.pool_label }
    gpu_type = var.gpu_type
    desired_count = var.desired_count
    taints = ["redwood-inference/gpu:NoSchedule"]
  }

- Remote state note: if TFE not permitted: backend = "s3" with server_side_encryption = "AES256" and dynamodb table for locks; for airgap provide manual lock/unlock SOP and require PR approval for apply.

End of draft.

Notes to self: keep this in-drive as the canonical Sable doc until architecture review. Expect customer security team to push back on any outbound NAT windows.
